pairs.locus: Florus, Epitome 1.13 (Bellum Tarentinum, on the Roman dead crushed by Pyrrhus' elephants)
pairs.question: Quinam illi fuerunt viri, quos ab elephantis primo proelio obtritos accepimus?
pairs.answer: Omnium volnera in pectore, quidam hostibus suis morte sua commortui, omnium in manibus ensis, et relictae in voltibus minae, et in ipsa morte ira vivebat.
pairs.derivation: Florus poses a genuine interrogative (Quinam illi fuerunt viri...?) and answers it himself by characterizing the men. Answer is the contiguous span describing them, ending at its full stop; the next sentence ('Quod adeo Pyrrhus miratus est...') turns to Pyrrhus' reaction and is excluded. No scaffolding or brackets in this span.

pairs.locus: Florus, Epitome 1.22 (Bellum Punicum secundum, Fabius' embassy declaring war on Carthage)
pairs.question: In hoc ego sinu bellum pacemque porto; utrum eligit?
pairs.derivation: Fabius asks a real interrogative offering war or peace (utrum eligit[is]?); the Carthaginians answer 'bellum.' Kept the setup sentence 'In hoc ego sinu bellum pacemque porto' so the choice has a referent. Dropped the speech-tag framing 'Fabius', 'inquit', and 'subclamantibus' (which narrates the shouted reply); kept only the answering word 'bellum'. Capitalized 'In' and 'Bellum' and added terminal '.'; text quoted verbatim including the printed 'eligit'.
